item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
085
ABPZ20 KNHC 160515
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Thu Oct 15 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Simon, located a few hundred miles south-southeast of the
southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula, and on Hurricane
Trudy, located a few hundred miles southwest of Acapulco, Mexico.

South of Southern Mexico:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form offshore of southern
Mexico during the early to middle part of next week. Environmental
conditions appear conducive for gradual development thereafter, and
a tropical depression could form during the latter half of next week
while it moves generally westward to west-northwestward over the
eastern and central portions of the East Pacific.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...60 percent.

$$
Forecaster Evans/Reinhart

item.description:
Issued at 1200 AM CST Fri Oct 16 2026 
549 
WTPZ31 KNHC 160547

BULLETIN
Hurricane Trudy Intermediate Advisory Number 11A
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
1200 AM CST Fri Oct 16 2026
 
...TRUDY RAPIDLY INTENSIFIES INTO A MAJOR HURRICANE...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1200 AM CST...0600 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...14.0N 102.4W
ABOUT 260 MI...420 KM SW OF ACAPULCO MEXICO
ABOUT 365 MI...590 KM SSE OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...120 MPH...195 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 310 DEGREES AT 6 MPH...9 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...957 MB...28.26 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...
* The coast of Mexico north of Punta San Telmo to Cabo Corrientes
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* The coast of Mexico from Punta San Telmo southward to Zihuatanejo
 
A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible 
within the watch area. A watch is typically issued 48 hours before 
the anticipated first occurrence of tropical-storm-force winds, 
conditions that make outside preparations difficult or dangerous.
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area within 36 hours.
 
Interests elsewhere in southwestern and west-central Mexico should 
continue monitor the progress of Trudy. Additional watches or 
warnings will likely be required later today.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1200 AM CST (0600 UTC), the eye of Hurricane Trudy was located 
near latitude 14.0 North, longitude 102.4 West. Trudy is moving 
toward the northwest near 6 mph (9 km/h). A north-northwestward 
motion is expected today, followed by a turn toward the northwest 
tonight or Saturday. On the forecast track, the center of Trudy will 
approach the coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico on 
Saturday and Saturday night.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 120 mph (195 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Trudy is a category 3 hurricane on the 
Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale. Additional strengthening is 
forecast during the next day or two.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 25 miles (35 km) from
the center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 105
miles (165 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 957 mb (28.26 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Trudy can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP1 and WMO header WTPZ41 KNHC
and on the web at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?key_messages.
 
WIND: Tropical storm conditions are expected within the tropical 
storm warning area by early Saturday. Hurricane conditions are 
possible in the hurricane watch area by Saturday night, with 
tropical storm conditions beginning on Saturday.
 
RAINFALL: Through the weekend, Trudy is expected to produce 4 to 8 
inches with isolated higher totals around 12 inches through the 
weekend along and near the coast of southwest Mexico in Michoacan, 
Colima and Jalisco. This rainfall may produce life-threatening 
flooding and mudslides, especially in areas along steep terrain.
 
Elsewhere, Trudy’s outer bands are expected to produce 2 to 4 inches 
with isolated higher totals around 6 inches along the southwest 
coast of Mexico in Guerrero. This rainfall may result in localized 
flash flooding through the weekend, especially in areas along steep 
terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Trudy,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?rainqpf.
 
STORM SURGE: Coastal flooding from storm surge is possible in areas
of onshore winds. Near the coast, the surge will be accompanied by
large and destructive waves.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Trudy will affect portions of the coast of
southwestern and west-central Mexico during the next few days. These
swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions. Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 AM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Reinhart

item.title: Hurricane Trudy Forecast Discussion Number 11
item.description:
Issued at 900 PM CST Thu Oct 15 2026 
410 
WTPZ41 KNHC 160247
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Trudy Discussion Number  11
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
900 PM CST Thu Oct 15 2026
 
The latest satellite imagery of Trudy continues to show a core of 
deep convection with cloud tops near -80C, particularly on the 
western side of the circulation. During the past few hours, an eye 
feature has become apparent on infrared and proxy-vis imagery. 
Unfortunately, there have not been any recent microwave passes to 
provide a better assessment of the core structure since the Air 
Force Hurricane Hunters departed earlier this afternoon. The latest 
subjective Dvorak satellite intensity estimate from TAFB is T5.0/90 
kt, while UW-CIMSS objective intensity estimates have a fairly large 
spread of 65-81 kt. Given the improved satellite presentation since 
the previous advisory, with an eye-like feature, and the TAFB 
classification, the initial intensity is raised to 90 kt.
 
The initial motion is north-northwestward, or 345/6 kt. Trudy is 
moving generally north-northwestward into a weakness in the 
subtropical ridge caused by an upper-level trough over the Yucatan 
Peninsula. As the trough moves eastward, the ridge is forecast to 
build over central Mexico, steering Trudy northwestward to 
north-northwestward along its western periphery and roughly parallel 
to the coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico. Most of the 
track guidance keeps the center just offshore, with the exception of 
the GFS, which brings the center inland. After 72 h, a mid-level 
ridge to the north of the system is expected to build, turning Trudy 
more westward. The latest NHC track forecast is very similar to the 
previous advisory through 60 h, but has been adjusted slightly north 
thereafter, leaning toward the HCCA and GDMI aids.
 
Environmental conditions are favorable for steady to rapid 
intensification during the next day or so. Sea surface temperatures 
are near 29-30C, combined with low vertical wind shear and abundant 
mid-level moisture. The NHC peak intensity forecast still remains at 
125 kt, which is above all the intensity guidance. The SHIPS Rapid 
Intensification (RI) index still shows a 20 to 30 percent chance of 
RI over the next 24 h, and the NHC forecast explicitly reflects RI 
during that time frame. After 36-48 h, increasing southwesterly wind 
shear, potential internal structural changes, such as eyewall 
replacement cycles, and land interaction will begin to disrupt the 
circulation, inducing a weakening trend. Regardless, Trudy is 
forecast to be a powerful major hurricane as it nears west-central 
Mexico. It is worth noting that the intensity forecast is highly 
sensitive to the exact track. A track farther to the left and 
offshore would allow Trudy to remain stronger than currently 
forecast, while a track that brings the center inland would result 
in rapid weakening. Beyond 72 h, strong shear should cause continued 
weakening, even though the system will have less land interaction as 
it moves farther offshore. The NHC intensity forecast lies near the 
upper end of the guidance initially, then trends toward the HCCA 
corrected consensus by the end of the forecast period.
   
KEY MESSAGES:
 
1. Trudy is forecast to be a major hurricane as it approaches the 
coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico this weekend, bringing 
an increasing risk of storm surge, damaging winds, and flooding 
rain. Hurricane Watches and Tropical Storm Warnings are currently in 
effect for portions of the coast, and additional watches and 
warnings will likely be required on Friday.
 
2. Heavy rainfall associated with Trudy will impact the southwest 
Mexican coast between Guerrero and Jalisco through the weekend. This 
rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides by the 
weekend along and near the southwest Mexican coast in Michoacán, 
Colima, and Jalisco, especially in areas along steep terrain.
 
3. Large swells will begin to affect portions of the coast of
southwestern Mexico Friday and continue through the weekend. These
swells could cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS

item.title: Tropical Storm Simon Forecast Discussion Number 36
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM MST Fri Oct 16 2026 
000
WTPZ45 KNHC 160840
TCDEP5
 
Tropical Storm Simon Discussion Number  36
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
200 AM MST Fri Oct 16 2026
 
Simon is gradually weakening. The storm continues to lose 
organization with intermittent bursts of deeper convection north of 
the center. A 0501 UTC Metop-C scatterometer pass showed a compact 
system with peak winds around 34 kt. Intensity estimates have 
dropped slightly, and the latest subjective Dvorak CI number from 
TAFB was 2.5/35 kt, but the Final T-number was 2.0/30 kt. Based on a 
compromise of these data, the initial intensity is lowered to 35 kt.
 
The initial motion is estimated to be northwesterly, or 310/08 kt. 
This general motion is forecast to continue through the weekend as 
the system moves in between a low-level trough to its west and a 
ridge to its east, bringing the weak and shallow system just west of 
the Baja California Peninsula over the weekend. The latest microwave 
and scatterometer data required a minor adjustment to the previous 
center position; therefore, the updated forecast track has been 
nudged northward accordingly, roughly between the corrected 
consensus (HCCA) and Google DeepMind (GDMI) ensemble.
 
Simon is anticipated to gradually weaken over the next 24–36 h due 
to an unfavorable environment of moderate to strong southwesterly 
vertical wind shear and dry mid-level air. As a result, Simon is 
expected to become a remnant low within 24 h and dissipate in about 
48 h.
